title: Product Formula: The Algebraic Heart of the CLT
content:
The product formula
  φ_{μ₁,σ₁²}(t) · φ_{μ₂,σ₂²}(t) = φ_{μ₁+μ₂,σ₁²+σ₂²}(t)
is a one-line consequence of exp(a)·exp(b) = exp(a+b):

  exp(iμ₁t - σ₁²t²/2) · exp(iμ₂t - σ₂²t²/2)
  = exp((iμ₁t - σ₁²t²/2) + (iμ₂t - σ₂²t²/2))
  = exp(i(μ₁+μ₂)t - (σ₁²+σ₂²)t²/2)
  = φ_{μ₁+μ₂,σ₁²+σ₂²}(t)

This encodes the fundamental fact: X₁ ~ N(μ₁,σ₁²) and X₂ ~ N(μ₂,σ₂²) independent implies X₁+X₂ ~ N(μ₁+μ₂,σ₁²+σ₂²). The power formula `gaussianCharFn_pow` follows by induction on this product.
mathContext: The characteristic function φ_X(t) = E[e^{itX}] transforms convolution (sum of independent r.v.) into pointwise multiplication. The Gaussian distribution is a fixed point of this multiplication structure: the family {N(μ,σ²)} is closed under convolution, with parameters adding. This is the algebraic core of the CLT.

title: |φ(t)| = exp(-σ²t²/2): Mean Affects Phase Only
content:
The modulus computation reveals a key structural fact:
  |φ_{μ,σ²}(t)| = |exp(iμt - σ²t²/2)|
                = exp(Re(iμt - σ²t²/2))
                = exp(-σ²t²/2)

The mean μ appears only in the imaginary part iμt of the exponent — it oscillates but doesn't decay. Only σ² controls the decay rate.

Consequences:
• |φ(t)| = 1 iff σ² = 0 (degenerate/point mass)
• For σ² > 0: |φ(t)| < 1 for all t ≠ 0
• The decay exp(-σ²t²/2) is integrable over ℝ → Lévy's inversion theorem applies
mathContext: For any z ∈ ℂ: |e^z| = e^{Re(z)}. The real part of the Gaussian exponent is -σ²t²/2 regardless of μ. This Gaussian envelope in frequency space is dual to the Gaussian density in physical space — the Fourier transform of e^{-σ²x²/2} is e^{-t²/(2σ²)}.

title: CLT Gaussian Stability: Sₙ/√n ~ N(0,1) from Char Fn Algebra
content:
The CLT stability theorem in 10 lines:

If X₁,...,Xₙ are iid N(0,1), then Sₙ = X₁+...+Xₙ ~ N(0,n) by the product formula.
The characteristic function of Sₙ/√n at t is the char fn of Sₙ at t/√n:
  φ_{0,n}(t/√n) = exp(-n·(t/√n)²/2) = exp(-n·t²/(2n)) = exp(-t²/2) = φ_{0,1}(t)

So Sₙ/√n has the same characteristic function as N(0,1) — hence the same distribution.

The Lean proof uses `Real.sq_sqrt` to justify √n² = n for natural n, then `field_simp` and `nlinarith` for the algebraic simplification.
mathContext: This is the Gaussian case of the CLT, where the limit distribution is Gaussian precisely because Gaussians are closed under convolution and scaling. The general CLT (non-Gaussian iid) requires Lévy's continuity theorem — pointwise convergence of char fns implies weak convergence. This theorem provides the base case and demonstrates the proof strategy.

title: Conjugate Symmetry: φ(-t) = conj(φ(t)) ↔ Real Distribution
content:
For any real-valued random variable X:
  E[e^{-itX}] = E[conj(e^{itX})] = conj(E[e^{itX}])

So φ(-t) = conj(φ(t)) is equivalent to X being real-valued.

For the Gaussian: φ_{μ,σ²}(-t) = exp(-iμt - σ²t²/2) = conj(exp(iμt - σ²t²/2)) = conj(φ_{μ,σ²}(t)).

Special case: for μ = 0 (centered), φ(t) = exp(-σ²t²/2) is real and positive — its imaginary part is 0. This is proved in `gaussianCharFn_real_of_centered`.
mathContext: The conjugate symmetry condition is a necessary criterion for characteristic functions of real distributions. The Gaussian satisfies it because the density (2πσ²)^{-1/2} e^{-(x-μ)²/(2σ²)} is real-valued. In Lean, this is proved via `Complex.star_def` and coordinate computations.
